sudo iptables -F && sudo iptables -X && sudo iptables -P INPUT ACCEPT && sudo iptables -P FORWARD ACCEPT && sudo iptables -P OUTPUT ACCEPT

⚠️ A quick heads-up before you do: this flushes all rules, deletes user-defined chains, and sets all default policies to ACCEPT — effectively disabling the host firewall. If you're running this over SSH on a remote machine, do it carefully (it's generally safe since policies become ACCEPT, but make sure that's actually what you want). You may also want to handle the `nat` and `mangle` tables separately if you need a full reset:

```
sudo iptables -t nat -F && sudo iptables -t nat -X
sudo iptables -t mangle -F && sudo iptables -t mangle -X
```
